title: Magnetic plate comprising permanent magnets and electropermanent magnets

features.item: A housing containing a displaceable magnet and pole shoes with workpiece contact surfaces.
features.quote: A magnetic plate or holder, especially for machine tools, of the type in which a magnetically attractable workpiece can be retained by magnetic force on the plate for a machining process, e.g. surface grinding, comprises a pole plate, a frame
features.note: The reference discloses a magnetic holder with a frame (housing) and pole plates/sole plate (pole shoes) for retaining a workpiece, but it does not explicitly state that the magnet within is displaceable.

features.item: A magnet displaceable along a direction between a gripping position and a release position.
features.note: The reference describes electropermanent magnets whose magnetic direction is reversible by electrical pulses, but not a physically displaceable magnet.

features.item: Pole shoes attached to the housing, each with a workpiece contact surface.
features.quote: A magnetic plate or holder, especially for machine tools, of the type in which a magnetically attractable workpiece can be retained by magnetic force on the plate for a machining process, e.g. surface grinding, comprises a pole plate, a frame
features.note: The reference describes a pole plate and a sole plate, which act as pole shoes, attached to a frame (housing) and used to retain a workpiece, implying contact surfaces.
features.refuted: Quote describes a magnetic plate with pole plate and frame, but does not mention pole shoes attached to housing with workpiece contact surfaces.

features.item: Pole shoes designed to guide a magnetic field portion to the workpiece contact surface.
features.quote: Within the frame there is disposed a stack of alternately hard magnetic material, magnets of high coercive force and magnetic cores of low coercive force provided with respective energizing coils.
features.note: The description of a magnetic stack within a frame and sole plate implies that these components are designed to guide the magnetic field to the workpiece.
features.refuted: Quote describes magnetic stack components within frame but does not mention pole shoes or their function in guiding magnetic field to workpiece contact surface.

features.item: A workpiece contact surface defining a contact surface angle of 170° to 190° with the displacement direction.
features.note: The reference does not describe any specific angles for workpiece contact surfaces or a displacement direction for a magnet.

features.item: A magnetic gripper with housing, displaceable magnet, and pole shoes where contact surface angle is 170° to 190° relative to displacement direction.
features.note: The reference does not describe a displaceable magnet or specific contact surface angles relative to a displacement direction.

features.item: A magnetic gripper system with a magnetic gripper and ferromagnetic workpiece, where magnet in gripping position presses workpiece against contact surfaces by magnetic force.
features.quote: A magnetic plate or holder, especially for machine tools, of the type in which a magnetically attractable workpiece can be retained by magnetic force on the plate for a machining process
features.note: The reference explicitly states that a magnetically attractable workpiece can be retained by magnetic force on the plate.

features.item: Housing extending along a longitudinal axis with displacement direction parallel to that axis.
features.note: The reference does not describe a longitudinal axis for the housing or a displacement direction for a magnet.

features.item: Pole shoes with an active structure for directing the magnetic field portion.
features.quote: a magnetic stack bridging said walls and in contact therewith, said magnetic stack comprising alternating highcoercive force magnets and low-coercive-force magnets with soft magnetic pole pieces disposed between them
features.note: The description of a magnetic stack with alternating magnets and soft magnetic pole pieces implies an active structure for directing the magnetic field.
features.refuted: Quote describes magnetic stack with pole pieces between magnets, not pole shoes with active structure for directing magnetic field.

features.item: An active structure with a bevel defining a bevel angle of 5° to 85° with the workpiece contact surface.
features.note: The reference does not describe any bevels or specific angles for the active structure or workpiece contact surface.

features.item: An active structure with multiple projections for directing magnetic field and forming the workpiece contact surface.
features.note: The reference describes pole pieces but does not specify multiple projections for directing the magnetic field or forming the contact surface.

features.item: Adjacent first and second projections with a recess between them, recess depth or length deviating by at most 25% from projection length.
features.note: The reference does not describe projections with recesses or their specific dimensions.

features.item: A positioning device on the magnetic gripper for positioning the ferromagnetic workpiece on the contact surface.
features.note: The reference describes retaining a workpiece but does not mention a specific positioning device.

features.item: First and second pole shoes where the magnet in gripping position makes the first pole shoe act as north pole and second as south pole.
features.quote: the electromagnetic cores are magnetized opposite the high-coercive-force hard magnetic members and, in the inoperative position of the magnetic plate, the magnetic cores are magnetized in the same sense as the hard magnetic bodies, thereby closing a magnetic short circuit
features.note: The reference describes the magnetization of cores and hard magnetic members in opposite senses to create a magnetic field, implying the creation of north and south poles.
features.refuted: Quote describes magnetization states in operative vs inoperative positions but does not mention first and second pole shoes acting as north and south poles in gripping position.

features.item: A magnet displaceable electrically, pneumatically, or mechanically between gripping and release positions.
features.quote: the magnetic direction of said low-coercive-force magnets being reversible by the application of electrical pulses to said coils.
features.note: The reference describes electrically reversible magnets, which achieve gripping and release, but not physical displacement of the magnet itself.

features.item: A position sensor detecting gripping position and/or release position, or a workpiece sensor detecting the ferromagnetic workpiece.
features.note: The reference does not mention any sensors for detecting position or workpiece presence.

features.item: Housing with a receptacle for receiving a workpiece sensor and/or a supply line.
features.note: The reference does not describe any receptacles for sensors or supply lines.

features.item: A manipulator interface on the magnetic gripper for attaching to a manipulator.
features.note: The reference describes a magnetic plate or holder for machine tools but does not mention a manipulator interface.

features.item: Housing portion designed to suppress magnetic field escape, or a shielding device to at least partially prevent magnetic field escape.
features.note: The reference describes the magnetic circuit but does not mention any features for suppressing magnetic field escape or shielding.

features.item: At least one projection with length deviating by at most 25% from the thickness of the ferromagnetic workpiece.
features.note: The reference does not describe any projections or their dimensions relative to a workpiece thickness.

features.item: A receptacle in the form of a groove in the housing.
features.note: The reference does not describe any grooves in the housing.

features.item: A bevel angle of 15° to 75° between the active structure bevel and the workpiece contact surface.
features.note: The reference does not describe any bevels or specific angles for the active structure or workpiece contact surface.

features.item: A bevel angle of 40° to 60° between the active structure bevel and the workpiece contact surface.
features.note: The reference does not describe any bevels or specific angles for the active structure or workpiece contact surface.

claims.quote: A magnetic plate or holder, especially for machine tools, of the type in which a magnetically attractable workpiece can be retained by magnetic force on the plate for a machining process, e.g. surface grinding, comprises a pole plate, a frame
claims.note: The reference discloses a magnetic holder for retaining a magnetically attractable workpiece, which is similar to a magnetic gripper for gripping a ferromagnetic workpiece. However, it does not explicitly mention a 'gripper' or the specific mechanism of gripping versus retaining.

The reference describes a magnetic stack with reversible magnetic direction, but it does not disclose a magnet that is displaceable along a displacement direction between gripping and release positions.

claims.quote: a pole plate having respective pole regions in contact with said pole pieces, said pole plate lying in contact with said walls.
claims.note: The reference discloses a pole plate with pole regions that guide a magnetic field, which is similar to pole shoes with workpiece contact surfaces. However, it does not explicitly state that these pole regions are 'attached to the housing' or that they have a 'workpiece contact surface' in the same way as described in the claim.
The reference does not disclose any information about a contact surface angle between a workpiece contact surface and a displacement direction.
This reference does not disclose any specific contact surface angle for a workpiece, nor does it mention a displacement direction for a magnet.
This reference describes a 'hollow body' or 'frame' but does not specify that it extends along a longitudinal axis.
This reference does not describe a displacement direction for a magnet, nor does it align such a direction with a longitudinal axis.

claims.note: The reference discloses pole pieces that are part of a magnetic stack and guide a magnetic field, which is a form of active structure. However, it does not explicitly state that each pole shoe has an active structure for directing the magnetic field portion, as the subject claim implies a specific design for the pole shoe itself.

The reference does not describe an active structure with a plurality of projections for directing a magnetic field portion or forming a workpiece contact surface.
The reference does not describe a plurality of projections, nor does it specify a first and second projection.
The reference does not describe a plurality of projections, nor does it specify a first and second projection that are adjacent to one another.
The reference does not describe an active structure with a recess between a first and second projection.
The reference does not describe a recess or its dimensions relative to projections.
This reference describes a magnetic plate for retaining a workpiece, but it does not disclose a specific positioning device for the workpiece.

claims.quote: a magnetic stack comprising alternating highcoercive force magnets and low-coercive-force magnets with soft magnetic pole pieces disposed between them, said pole pieces being spaced above said sole plate
claims.note: The reference discloses soft magnetic pole pieces, which are analogous to pole shoes, but it does not specify a first and second pole shoe explicitly.

claims.quote: In the inoperative position of the magnetic plate, the magnetic cores are magnetized in the same sense as the hard magnetic bodies, thereby closing a magnetic short circuit field through the stack, the frame and the sole plate.
claims.note: The reference describes the magnetization of the magnetic cores and hard magnetic bodies, which implies the creation of north and south poles, but it does not explicitly state that a first pole shoe acts as a north pole and a second pole shoe acts as a south pole in a gripping position.

claims.quote: the magnetic direction of said low-coercive-force magnets being reversible by the application of electrical pulses to said coils.
claims.note: The reference discloses that the magnetic direction of the low-coercive-force magnets is reversible by electrical pulses, which allows for switching between an operative and inoperative position. However, it does not explicitly state that the magnet itself is displaceable electrically, pneumatically, or mechanically.
This reference does not mention a position sensor for detecting gripping or release positions.
This reference does not mention a workpiece sensor for detecting a ferromagnetic workpiece.
This reference does not describe a housing with a receptacle for a workpiece sensor or a supply line.

claims.quote: A magnetic plate or holder, especially for machine tools, of the type in which a magnetically attractable workpiece can be retained by magnetic force on the plate for a machining process, e.g. surface grinding, comprises a pole plate, a frame
claims.note: The reference describes a magnetic plate or holder with soft magnetic materials (frame and sole plate) which can help to guide or contain the magnetic field, but it does not explicitly state that these components are designed to largely suppress the escape of the magnetic field from the housing portion.

claims.quote: A magnetic plate or holder, especially for machine tools, of the type in which a magnetically attractable workpiece can be retained by magnetic force on the plate for a machining process, e.g. surface grinding, comprises a pole plate, a frame

claims.quote: A magnetic plate or holder, especially for machine tools, of the type in which a magnetically attractable workpiece can be retained by magnetic force on the plate for a machining process, e.g. surface grinding, comprises a pole plate, a frame

claims.quote: A magnetic plate or holder, especially for machine tools, of the type in which a magnetically attractable workpiece can be retained by magnetic force on the plate for a machining process, e.g. surface grinding, comprises a pole plate, a frame
claims.note: The reference describes a 'magnetic plate or holder' (magnetic gripper) and a 'magnetically attractable workpiece'.
claims.refuted: The quote describes a magnetic plate system but makes no reference to 'claim 5' or any specific claim dependency structure.

claims.quote: A magnetic plate or holder, especially for machine tools, of the type in which a magnetically attractable workpiece can be retained by magnetic force on the plate for a machining process
claims.note: This passage describes a magnetic holder retaining a workpiece by magnetic force, which implies a gripping state where the workpiece is pressed against the surface.
claims.refuted: The quote mentions magnetic retention but does not describe a 'gripping state,' 'gripping position,' or workpieces being 'pressed against contact surfaces.'

claims.quote: In the inoperative position of the system, the electromagnetic cores are magnetized opposite the high-coercive-force hard magnetic members
claims.note: This describes an 'inoperative position' where the magnetic cores are magnetized oppositely, which would lead to a reduced or cancelled magnetic force, effectively releasing the workpiece.
claims.refuted: The quote describes an 'inoperative position' with magnetization states, not a 'release position' where workpiece is not pressed against contact surfaces.

The reference does not describe any receptacle in the form of a groove.
